evidence.excerpt: Relation extraction between biomedical entities in low-resource languages is typically approached by adapting English-trained models, but direct adaptation is complicated by the absence of parallel corpora and the syntactic differences of inflected languages. This preprint describes a lightweight relation extraction pipeline applied to a set of 620 Serbian clinical case reports collected from three open-access Serbian medical journals between 2015 and 2025. The pipeline uses the disease and gene named entity recogniser developed in prior work, extended here with a drug entity module trained on a manually annotated set of 300 sentences. Candidate drug–disease pairs are classified using a support vector machine over typed dependency features extracted from a Serbian dependency parser. The approach avoids large model fine-tuning and can run on CPU hardware. On a held-out set of 80 case reports, the pipeline identifies drug–disease treatment relations with a precision of 0.72 and recall of 0.61. Error analysis indicates that the main precision losses arise from non-treatment drug mentions such as contraindications mentioned in passing. The code and evaluation data are shared as a preprint to invite community feedback before journal submission.
